questiontext.text: Passage: A character gives up a winning speech slot to help a nervous friend prepare. What universal theme is best supported?

answer.text: Personal goals can still leave room for helping others.

questiontext.text: Source element: A guide gives an object before a journey. Adaptation: A coach gives a route card before a city race. What is preserved?

answer.text: A guide supports a journey with an object.

questiontext.text: Central idea: Avoiding responsibility can make guilt grow. Which detail best supports it?

answer.text: The character hides the broken key after blaming someone else.

questiontext.text: Passage: "Naturally, the committee solved the leak by buying a larger bucket." What rhetorical choice is strongest?
Passage: Eli thinks family stories delay chores until he finds the same street names in his grandmother's old notebook. What changes?

answer.text: Eli recognizes that the stories carry family history.

questiontext.text: Passage A: Lina practices alone after failure. Passage B: Theo asks for help after failure. What comparison is strongest?

answer.text: The passages are identical because both have names.
Both show growth after failure, but one emphasizes independent persistence while the other emphasizes support.

questiontext.text: Passage: Talia thinks asking for critique proves weakness, but later asks what to revise first. What coming-of-age change is shown?

answer.text: She learns feedback can be part of growth.

questiontext.text: What is a complete theme statement?

answer.text: Friendship can require honesty even when honesty is uncomfortable.

questiontext.text: A student adapts a source by changing only character names while keeping the exact plot and ending. What is the problem?

answer.text: It is too close to copying and lacks meaningful transformation.

questiontext.text: Passage: The clock ticks louder each time Ren avoids the question. What is the reader effect?

answer.text: The sound detail increases tension around avoidance.

questiontext.text: Central idea: Memory can make a new place feel less lonely. Which revision best supports it?

answer.text: Change "blue rug" to "a blue rug the same color as Grandma's kitchen rug."

questiontext.text: Passage: A narrator repeats "not yet" while postponing the truth. What author purpose is likely?

answer.text: To prove the truth was told early.

questiontext.text: Which detail best supports "courage can exist beside fear"?

answer.text: Kai steps forward while hiding shaking hands.

questiontext.text: Source element: A forbidden door tests curiosity. Adaptation: A student is warned not to open a locked digital folder. What is preserved?
Passage: A character returns a trophy after learning the score was wrong. What theme is strongest?

answer.text: Doing what is right can matter more than public praise.

questiontext.text: Which explanation best connects evidence to central idea? Central idea: Secrets damage trust. Detail: The character deletes a message before a friend sees it.

answer.text: It supports the idea because phones exist.
The deleted message supports the idea because hiding communication creates secrecy between friends.
It supports the idea because it is a sentence.

questiontext.text: Passage: "Of course the award went to the student who arrived late and bowed like royalty." What tone is created?
What should a rationale for adaptation include?

answer.text: Source element, transformation, and reason for the change.

questiontext.text: Passage: A character thinks leadership means doing everything alone, then succeeds only after trusting the team. What central idea is best supported?
Passage: A narrator leaves home but packs a recipe card first. What theme is best supported?

answer.text: Change can include carrying meaningful parts of the past forward.

questiontext.text: What is a blind spot in coming-of-age fiction?

answer.text: Something a character does not yet understand.

questiontext.text: Passage: The writer gives the antagonist a quiet moment helping a child. What purpose might this serve?

answer.text: To prove the character has no role.
To change the passage into a recipe.
To complicate the reader's view of the character.

questiontext.text: Which comparison is strongest? Passage A: a child returns a stolen coin. Passage B: a merchant corrects an overpayment.

answer.text: Both develop integrity through returning what does not belong to the character.

questiontext.text: Scene plan: central idea about belonging, conflict about exclusion, and detail of a shared table. What makes it integrated?

answer.text: The conflict and table detail both support the belonging idea.

questiontext.text: A student writes, "The theme is that Kai finds a coin." What feedback is best?

answer.text: Revise because that is a plot detail; explain the larger idea the coin supports.
Keep it because all plot details are themes.

questiontext.text: Passage: Lena wanted to ignore the new student because everyone else did. At lunch, she moved her tray to the empty seat beside him. Which theme statement is strongest?

answer.text: Belonging often begins when one person chooses kindness over comfort.

questiontext.text: Passage: Tomas wanted to win the art prize, but he helped his tired partner finish her mural before starting his own final details. What topic and theme are best supported?

answer.text: Topic: ambition and teamwork; Theme: Personal goals can still leave room for helping others.
Topic: prizes; Theme: Prizes always ruin friendships.

questiontext.text: Passage: Asha kept the cracked bracelet after her friend moved away. She wore it on the first day at a new school, touching it before she introduced herself. What does the bracelet help develop?

answer.text: A theme about memory giving strength during change.
A rule that all bracelets are cracked.
A summary that Asha has a bracelet.

questiontext.text: Passage A: Rina gave her last pencil to a classmate before the exam. Passage B: Omar shared his umbrella even though his own sleeve got soaked. What shared theme is best supported?

answer.text: School supplies and umbrellas are the same object.
Weather is always more important than school.
Helping others can require giving up personal comfort or convenience.

questiontext.text: Passage A: Mina apologized after blaming her brother for the spill. Passage B: Carter returned the borrowed book after pretending he had lost it. How are the themes similar?

answer.text: Both show that honesty can repair damage after a mistake.

questiontext.text: Source element: A character receives a warning before making a risky choice. Adaptation: A student ignores a teammate's warning about faulty robot code before the final round. What is preserved?
Source element: A guide gives a traveler a protective object. Adaptation: A grandmother gives a narrator a recipe card before the narrator moves to a new city. What is transformed?

answer.text: The protective object becomes emotional support through a recipe card.

questiontext.text: Central idea: Avoiding responsibility can make guilt grow. Passage detail: Niko hides the baseball under three blankets after blaming the broken window on the wind. How does the detail support the central idea?

answer.text: It proves the wind broke the window.
It distracts from the central idea completely.
It shows Niko's guilt growing through secretive action.

questiontext.text: Central idea: Accepting help can be a form of strength. Which detail best supports the idea?

answer.text: The character describes an unrelated poster for three paragraphs.
The character refuses all help and leaves.
The character hands one heavy box to a friend and keeps walking beside her.

questiontext.text: Passage: The writer repeats the image of an empty chair at dinner before explaining who is missing. What is the most likely purpose?

answer.text: To make the reader feel absence before receiving full explanation.

questiontext.text: Passage: "Of course the award went to the student who forgot the speech and bowed like royalty." What craft choice is strongest?

Passage: Talia thinks asking for critique proves she is not ready for advanced art. After her teacher explains that artists revise through feedback, Talia asks what to change first. What is Talia's changed understanding?

answer.text: Feedback can be part of serious growth.

questiontext.text: Passage: Marco thinks his father's traffic rules are about control. After his sister almost rides into the street, he understands why his father checks twice. What causes Marco's change?

answer.text: He sees the safety reason behind the rule.

questiontext.text: Scene plan: Central idea: maturity includes accepting guidance. Source influence: a guide gives an object before a journey. Character conflict: Maya thinks leaders work alone, while her teammate thinks leaders trust the group. Which choice best explains integration?

answer.text: The plan is integrated because every element supports shared responsibility.
The plan is integrated because it has many unrelated parts.
The source influence distracts because objects can never develop theme.
The conflict should be removed so the theme is easier.

questiontext.text: Passage: Jalen believed the mural had to be his design alone. When Amara handed him a sketch showing how everyone's ideas could fit, he erased his signature from the center and redrew the wall as a shared map. What changed understanding is shown?

answer.text: Jalen learns that leadership can include shared creative ownership.
